summary: Module 5 FIX (Recognize and Recover): at the regression point, the two-iteration rule says RESTART, not one more refinement. Option 2 chosen -- restart from clean context. My real M2 schema-conflict restart is the canonical example of this exact decision: the corrected Task 2 prompt was NOT 'the connection is broken, fix it' -- it embedded the interface contract verbatim (actual Task 1 output: created_by not owner_id, team_members join table, role values, permission rule, 409/404 codes) plus the preventative rule 'never prompt from plan assumptions, only from upstream actual output'. That restart prompt was significantly better than the original because it encoded what the failed iteration taught me. Why not Option 1 (targeted refinement): the regression was structural (schema contract mismatch / agent holding conflicting context), and a targeted patch on top of accumulated context would compound the pollution -- exactly the module's lesson. SHIPPED: all verification scenarios re-run and passing -- (a) round-trip probe: create team 201, add member 201, owner list 200 with member present, invite 201 pending; (b) IDOR 9-case probe: non-member 403 on create/list/revoke, dup 409, revoke 204, accept-once 200, replay 400, revoked 400; (c) contract check: created_by intact, owner-not-in-members, roles admin/member, constraints intact; (d) full suite 92 green. The ship-it discipline: if anything had failed I would have documented it rather than pretending; nothing did. THE LESSON I AM CARRYING FORWARD: persistence past the convergence point is actively harmful with AI agents -- the quality trajectory is the data, and a well-informed restart beats a polluted spiral every time.
evidence: M2 restart prompt embedded interface contract verbatim (created_by, team_members, role values, permission rule, 409/404) + preventative rule
